## ERCOT Hourly Load and Temperature Panel {#sec-data-ercot-shaffer}

These data were assembled to characterize the relationship between temperature
and electricity demand in Texas. The panel links hourly zone-level load from
ERCOT with hourly surface temperature observations from nearby weather stations,
enabling temperature response functions to be estimated separately for each of
ERCOT's eight weather zones. @ercot-shaffer uses these data to examine how
the load–temperature relationship changed over time, estimating the functions
across rolling multi-year windows from 2002 through 2020.

**Resources:**

- [Article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2589004222004436)
- [Replication archive](https://github.com/blakeshaffer/ercotproject)

**Provenance.** Load data originate from the Electric Reliability Council of Texas
(ERCOT) and reflect hourly settlement-point electricity demand, in megawatts, for
each of ERCOT's eight weather zones from January 2002 through March 2021. Temperature
data originate from NOAA's Local Climatological Data (LCD) product, which reports
hourly observations from Automated Surface Observing System (ASOS) and Automated
Weather Observing System (AWOS) stations. NOAA LCD reports dry-bulb temperature
in **degrees Fahrenheit** for U.S. stations; the field name `HourlyDryBulbTemperature`
is the exact column name used in LCD exports. One representative station was
selected per ERCOT weather zone. The two sources are matched on datetime and zone.
Large-scale load-shed events (outages) are flagged from ERCOT operating records to
allow their exclusion from estimation. All data were curated by Blake Shaffer and
are archived at the replication repository above. See @ercot-shaffer for the primary
citation.

### Variables {.unnumbered}

| Variable | Type | Unit / Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DATEHOUR` | Datetime | Hourly | Timestamp of the observation, UTC. Identifies the hour of load measurement and temperature reading; used as the join key between load, weather, and outage data. |
| `LOCATION` | Categorical | — | ERCOT weather zone name. Eight zones: Coast (Houston), East (Tyler), Far West (Midland), North (Wichita Falls), North Central (DFW), South (Corpus Christi), South Central (Austin), West (Abilene). Used as a grouping variable; all regressions are estimated within zone. |
| `LOAD` | Continuous | MW | Hourly electricity demand for the weather zone, in megawatts. This is the outcome variable in the temperature response function regressions. |
| `HourlyDryBulbTemperature` | Continuous | °F | Hourly dry-bulb surface air temperature from the nearest NOAA ASOS/AWOS station. **Values are in degrees Fahrenheit** (NOAA LCD native units). The key predictor in all analyses; in the published paper these are converted to Celsius before modeling, but are retained in Fahrenheit in the current working script. |
| `Outage` | Binary | 0 / 1 | Indicator for hours affected by large-scale, operator-initiated load shedding, sourced from ERCOT operating records. Flagged events include February 2008 and February 2011. Observations with `Outage == 1` are excluded from all regression estimation to avoid conflating involuntary curtailment with normal demand response. Not used in the current `test.R` exploratory plots but retained in the merged dataset. |
